j201.text: Last time, bread mould grew in our bag: a harmful fungus. Yeast made dough rise: a useful fungus. Then we washed our hands. Why?

j202.text: They look clean. I see nothing on them!

j203.text: Look closer, Pip. We need a microscope!

j254.text: The whole chapter on one map.

j301.text: Lock in first. And find the new lizard!

j401.text: A microscope allows us to see very small things.

j402.text: As scientists developed more powerful microscopes, they were able to discover living things that are even smaller than fungi.

j405.text: Bacteria are tiny living things and they come in different shapes and sizes.

j501.text: Be a bacterium! Shrink down. Quietly.

j502.text: You are one bacterium. Rod-shaped. Far too small to see.

j503.text: You sit on a fingertip. Its lines are like hills.

j504.text: It is recess. The hand reaches for a sandwich.

j505.text: But first: water! Soap! The bubbles lift you off.

j506.text: Whoosh! Down the drain you go.

j507.text: Now the hand is ready for food.

j601.text: Bacteria can be harmful when they cause you to fall sick.

j602.text: So wash your hands with soap before you eat.

j701.text: Round one. Are all bacteria harmful? One, yes. Two, no. Show me with your fingers.

j703.text: One! Bacteria make us sick. Wash them all away!

j704.text: Two! Some fungi are useful. Maybe some bacteria are too.

j705.text: Two. I think my yoghurt has some.

j708.text: Some bacteria are harmful, while others are useful to us.

j709.text: Useful bacteria in our body help us to break down food.

j710.text: Yoghurt and yoghurt drinks have useful bacteria like these.

j801.text: Pip's homework! Read the table. A has spores, and makes its own food. B has spores, and cannot make its own food. C has feathers, and cannot make its own food.

j802.text: My answers. One: A is a fungus. Two: B is a fungus. Three: C is a bird.

j803.text: Showdown! Double points. One line has a mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

j805.text: One! A makes its own food. So A is a plant, like a fern!

j806.text: One! Spores alone do not decide.

j808.text: Read every column. Spores, and cannot make its own food: a fungus.

j809.text: One finger? Put up two more on your score hand!

j901.text: Now, the whole chapter on one map! Living things.

j903.text: Animals: amphibians, birds, fish, insects, reptiles, mammals.

j905.text: Fungi and bacteria are also living things.

c1003.text: Fungi! Cannot make their own food! Bacteria! Tiny living things! Useful or harmful? Both can be!

j1103.text: Living things can be classified based on common observable characteristics. Scientists have classified different living things into groups such as plants, animals, fungi and bacteria.

j1201.text: Show me your score hand! More than one? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

j1202.text: Did you spot the lizard? It was on the kitchen clock. Can you see a lizard without a microscope? Tell someone at home.

j1301.text: Next time, something new: materials! A plastic box, a metal box and a glass jar. One of them was made from sand. Which one? Lock in your answer!

j1302.text: Sand? In my snack box? Crunchy!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
